reading.body:
Deb Fischer's recorded AI record is one bill and two PAC checks, not a broad pattern of AI legislation.

The fourteen events are almost entirely a single bill, S. 2296, across ten amendment and procedural votes on October 9, 2025, plus three earlier procedural votes in September. She voted Yea on final passage and on two amendments, and Nay on six others. The data does not name what any amendment would have done, so the votes cannot be read as positions on AI policy specifically.

The money is two contributions of $2,500 each, from Meta Platforms PAC in December 2025 and Amazon's PAC in February 2025. Both are the same amount, and both come from committees rather than the companies directly. Two data points cannot establish a donor relationship, and the page itself states it draws no conclusion about causation or motive.

What this record does not contain is as important as what it does. There are no sponsored AI bills, no committee assignments, no hearings, and no events after December 2025. For a question about AI and the grid, compute buildout, or data center power, this data offers nothing at all. It covers votes and contributions, and only those.
